//: Static CLI security tools shipped in the pack's bin/ dir. build_pack.py resolves each
//2: entry for the target (os,arch), downloads it, extracts the named binary, and records
//3: the observed sha256 into tools.lock.json for reproducible offline verification.
//4: URL templates use {version} {os} {arch} {arch2}; per-tool os/arch maps normalise naming.
//5: A tool with no build for a given (os,arch) is skipped (logged), never fatal.

tools.//: Fast SYN/CONNECT port scanner. Complements nmap: naabu sweeps the whole
tools.//2: port range in seconds, nmap then service-probes the open ones.
tools.//3: SYN mode (`-s s`, the default) needs libpcap AND root/cap_net_raw, neither of
tools.//4: which a portable pack can ship -- same constraint as nmap's -sS. CONNECT mode
tools.//5: (`-s c`) is the unprivileged path and is what agents should use, mirroring
tools.//6: nmap -sT. Go static binary, so no libpcap is needed for connect scans.
tools.name: naabu

tools.//: Crawler/spider -- URL + endpoint discovery to feed httpx/nuclei/ffuf. The
tools.//2: default standard mode is pure Go (no browser); `-headless` needs a Chromium
tools.//3: the base pack does not ship (see the README's tier-2 browser pack), so it
tools.name: katana

tools.//: TLS/cert grabber with real cipher-suite and protocol enumeration
tools.//3: This closes a documented gap: strobes_net/tls.py states cipher-suite
tools.//4: enumeration is impossible in the pack because the bundled nmap ships
tools.//5: WITHOUT nse_main.lua, so `--script ssl-enum-ciphers` dies and only the
tools.//6: single negotiated protocol/cipher is observable. tlsx does the full
tools.//7: enumeration itself in Go, no NSE and no OpenSSL needed.
tools.name: tlsx
nmap
tools.//: Linux: ernw portable nmap is musl-static (runs on ANY Linux incl. Alpine/old-
tools.//2: glibc, no floor). Flat archive: nmap/ncat/nping + data/. NMAPDIR -> data.
tools.//3: Connect scan (-sT) unprivileged; SYN (-sS)/OS-detect need root/cap_net_raw.

tools.name: nmap
tools.//: Windows: last portable win32 zip (nmap stopped shipping it after 7.92). nmap.exe
tools.//2: needs its adjacent DLLs, so the whole dir goes on PATH (not symlinked out).
tools.//3: Data files at bundle root -> NMAPDIR=share/nmap. Connect scans (-sT) work; SYN/
tools.//4: OS-detect need the Npcap driver, a privileged kernel install nmap can't bundle.

tools.name: nmap
tools.//: macOS: upstream ships only a .dmg installer. The builder mounts it, expands the
tools.//2: mpkg and extracts nmap/ncat/nping + data. The binary is x86_64 (native on Intel,
tools.//3: Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon) and statically links all but libSystem/libc++.
tools.//4: Connect scan (-sT) works unprivileged; SYN/OS-detect need sudo. Built on macOS only.

tools.//2: a .pkg -- so this needs build_pack's `pkg` branch (pkgutil --expand-full,
tools.//3: which unpacks the payload without touching the system). The binary is a
tools.//4: UNIVERSAL Mach-O (x86_64 + arm64), so one asset serves both arches, and
tools.//5: it carries its own Python alongside -- hence bundle, not a bare binary.
tools.name: aws
